messages:
deploy-bot: :rotating_light: Canary deploy completed to canary pool 'svc-canary-03' (model: redwood-open-3b@v7, sha:abc123). Observability: tokenization_error_rate spike +42%, malformed token sequences rising, 5xxs up 8%. Paging oncall.

alice (eng-runtime): saw the page. pulling logs from canary nodes now. can someone paste the exact failing API call payloads?

ben (oncall): i'm up — taking this. ben oncall here, started collecting traces. canary node ids?

carol (sre): node list from deploy: canary-3a, canary-3b, canary-3c. system load normal. errors look like tokenizer produced unexpected <UNK> tokens mid-sentence. sample attached in logs.

frank (ml-engineer): initial hunch: tokenizer metadata mismatch between weights and tokenizer config. v7 weights expect bytepair vocab v2 but deployed tokenizer config still v1. that would explain token boundaries and long-token splits.

eve (support): from support queue: ~12 orgs reported garbled completions in the last 10m, 2 of them on paid infra. one customer (acme-corp) says completions contain repeated strange unicode chars.

alice (eng-runtime): grabbing model artifacts on node: weight hash=sha:abc123, tokenizer metadata hash in environment = tok:v1-202505. model metadata expects tok:v2-202602. how did the deploy pipeline pass this?

incident-bot: paging carol, ben, alice, frank for incident-critical. escalation level: P1. Pager history: page sent to ben at 1765432202.

ben (oncall): i'm coordinating. frank, can you confirm whether the weights bundle contains the tokenizer files or if tokenizer is a separate artifact?

frank (ml-engineer): tokenizer is a separate artifact in our artifact registry. deploy job should pull both, but the canary config used an older artifact tag. i've reproduced locally: load v7 weights + v1 tokenizer -> tokenization errors + invalid token ids.

carol (sre): can we flip the feature flag to force canary to use previous model variant (v6) while we investigate? we should avoid immediate rollback until we assess impact.

alice (eng-runtime): flag path: /flags/model_routing/canary_override. current value: null. proposing set to "redwood-open-3b@v6".

ben (oncall): doing it now. command: 
```
flagsctl set /flags/model_routing/canary_override redwood-open-3b@v6 --author ben --reason "tokenizer mismatch on v7 canary"
```

ben (oncall): :white_check_mark: flag set. routing now diverted to v6 for new canary requests. monitoring for error rate drop.

eve (support): customer update: sent an interim message to affected orgs explaining we're investigating, asking for request ids. no escalations to legal.

dave (product): what's the customer-impact window? need to know if any SLOs were breached and whether to trigger credits.

frank (ml-engineer): based on logs, impacted window ~1765432140 -> 1765432225 (approx 1.5m). ~4500 requests, errorful completions ~7% of those => ~315 bad completions. 2 paying customers had degraded outputs.

alice (eng-runtime): rolling metrics: tokenization_error_rate back to baseline in 90s after flag flip. latency normalized. looks like mitigation succeeded for new traffic. existing in-flight requests still noisy.

carol (sre): agree mitigation worked. recommend rollback of v7 from canary and hold on promoting to prod. frank, can we validate artifact tags and add a quick preflight check in pipeline to assert tokenizer metadata hash equality with weights metadata?

frank (ml-engineer): yes. i can add a verification step: compare weights.metadata.tokenizer_hash == tokenizer.metadata.hash before completing deploy. will open PR.

ben (oncall): performing canary rollback now to purge v7 completely. command: 
```
redwoodctl rollback --env canary --target sha:previous --confirm --force-restart
```

ben (oncall): rollback submitted. watchlist on nodes.

incident-bot: rollback job started (job id: rb-20260315-447). estimated completion 60s.

alice (eng-runtime): rollback completed, canary nodes now back to redwood-open-3b@v6. running validation suite against canary. all tokenization tests passing.

dave (product): thanks team. i'll coordinate customer comms & legal liaison. eve, please compile a list of affected accounts and their owners.

eve (support): on it. exporting affected request ids + org ids now, will post secure spreadsheet link in #customer-impact later.

frank (ml-engineer): PR for artifact-checker opened: https://git.internal/redwood/infra/merge/1234 — includes tokenizer hash compare and a hard fail for mismatches. also adding a follow-up job to scan past deployments for inconsistent pairs.

carol (sre): action items: 1) keep canary pinned to v6 until gated tests pass (alice). 2) add preflight artifact check (frank). 3) postmortem and timeline (ben & dave). 4) tighten deploy job to not allow separate artifact tags without explicit confirm (alice).

ben (oncall): handing off to carol for ongoing postmortem and follow-ups. i'm off call at 1765432300. thanks.

carol (sre): taking primary. will schedule incident review in the morning. preliminary severity: SEV2 (customer-impacting but containment achieved quickly). tagging for oncall review, ML review, and release engineering.

dave (product): leaving notes for comms: be transparent, emphasize quick mitigation and change to pipeline checks. will draft follow-up.

frank (ml-engineer): putting a short repro + mitigation guide in the incident doc so devs know how to verify artifacts locally.

incident-bot: incident record created: IR-2026-03-15-78. links: /incidents/IR-2026-03-15-78. next: postmortem due in 72h.

carol (sre): closing live thread. any more on-call tasks, reopen. good job all. :tada:
